# Comet 67P in 3D

Put on your red-and-blue glasses to float alongside Comet 67P, a bizarre rubber-duck-shaped world where two lobes—one twice the size of the other—are connected by a narrow neck, all while jets of icy material blast outward from its surface as it approaches the Sun. The European Rosetta spacecraft captured these images in 2015 from 114 miles away, creating a stunning three-dimensional window into one of the solar system's most active and strangely shaped visitors.
